articles.title: Bun 1.2: A Big Step Forward for the Fast JS/TS Runtime
articles.description: The JavaScriptCore-based Bun continues to up its server-side runtime game with strides forward in Node.js compatibility, performance boosts, and new APIs for interacting with S3 and S3-like object stores as well as Postgres. If you’d prefer to be ▶️ introduced to Bun 1.2 with a keynote-style video, it's a good watch.
articles.author: Ashcon Partovi and the Bun Team

articles.title: 🤖 Transformers.js v3.3: Machine Learning and AI for the Web
articles.description: This is a dry release announcement but I wanted to highlight the rapid pace that this exciting library is making for browser-based NLP, speech recognition, vision, and now text-to-speech use cases (live TTS demo here - it takes a while to load though). It’s also being used in Firefox for various enhancements (see below).
articles.author: Hugging Face

articles.title: 🕒 JavaScript Temporal is Coming (For Real!)
articles.description: We first mentioned the Temporal API proposal providing a better way to handle dates and times in JavaScript almost five years ago (in issue 496!) but now it really is almost here. Brian explains its basic concepts and where initial support is starting to appear.
articles.author: Brian Smith

articles.title: Avoiding anys with Linting and TypeScript
articles.description: any is TypeScript’s famous type fallback/safety hatch but if you can avoid it, you can benefit more from TypeScript’s type-checking features. Josh shares some tips to do just that.
articles.author: Josh Goldberg

articles.title: 🤖 Running Inference in Web Extensions
articles.description: Firefox Nightly is shipping with a new API that can let you use their AI runtime for offline machine learning tasks in Web extensions you create. It uses the previously mentioned Transformers.js and is already used in Firefox 133 to provide alt text for images in PDFs.
articles.author: Tarek Ziadé (Mozilla)

articles.title: deck.gl 9.1: GPU-Powered Large Scale Data Visualization
articles.description: deck.gl provides a way to create complex yet high performance data visualizations composed of multiple layers (examples). It can be used in a vanilla JS way or through React components and it’s ready for WebGPU.
articles.author: OpenJS Foundation

articles.title: ArkType 2.0: Runtime Validation Library
articles.description: An easy-to-deploy solution for schema validation that can infer TypeScript definitions 1:1 and use them as optimized validators for your data, both at runtime and for immediate type-level feedback in your editor.
articles.author: ArkType

articles.title: NodeBB v4.0.0 Released: Node.js Powered Forums
articles.description: Offers a classic forum experience in a modern Node.js-shaped guise. v4 adds support for federation between instances and the wider 'fediverse.'
articles.author: NodeBB, Inc.

articles.title: SRCL: Build React Apps with 'Terminal Aesthetics'
articles.description: The homepage is a live demonstration of what SRCL has to offer. It’s a suite of React components and styling to recreate a monospaced, terminal-like atmosphere
articles.author: Internet Development Studio Company

articles.title: 🎶 Chiptune.js: Module / Tracker File Player
articles.description: A library for playing ‘module’ music files like MOD, XM and S3M. (Demo.)
articles.author: Chiptune Contributors

articles.description: The creator of SolidJS says that Angular and Vue are the frameworks to watch in 2025, while reflecting on JS framework progress generally.
A year ago, Kelly Sutton wrote about his company's move away from React but how did it pan out? In Moving On from React, a Year Later he explains how things have gone since.
JSON Query is a neat, flexible JSON querying language. The demos really sell it IMHO.
The ESLint project takes a look back at ESLint's 2024 year in review.
GitHub has unveiled sub-issues, issue types, and advanced search for issues.
Rspack v1.2 – Fast Rust-based Web bundler adds a peristent cache feature that improves hot start performance by up to 250%.
Node v23.6.1 (Current), v22.13.1 (LTS), v20.18.2 (LTS), v18.20.6 (LTS) to resolve some security vulnerabilities.
Capacitor 7.0 – Build cross-platform native apps/PWAs with web technologies.
React Native 0.77 – Now with enhanced styling capabilities.
Vitest 3.0 – The fast Vite-native testing framework.
NestJS 11, Storybook 8.5, Unpic 1.0, Inferno 9.0

articles.title: Tailwind CSS v4.0
articles.description: An all-new, ground-up rewrite of the highly popular framework. Version 4 arrived just after we hit send last week — it’s “optimized for performance and flexibility”, takes full advantage of modern web platform features, and is now CSS-first, moving away from a JS-based configuration. There’s lot of detail to dig into here.
articles.author: Adam Wathan

articles.title: Interop 2024 Brings More Features to Baseline
articles.description: We recently shared Jen Simmons’ report from the WebKit team on the progress made across the Interop project last year, now it’s the turn of Rachel Andrew of the Chrome team to look “back at the most successful year ever for the project”.
articles.author: Rachel Andrew

articles.title: Revisiting CSS Multi-Column Layout
articles.description: Andy explores the somewhat underused Multi-Column Layout module, looking at its history, limitations, and modern, practical uses. We also see how features like :has() selectors and container queries now make it a rather powerful tool.
articles.author: Andy Clarke

articles.title: Build for the Web, Build on the Web, Build with the Web
articles.description: Harry reminds us to take advantage of the “un-versioned by design” web platform: “What’s brand new today starts to show its age much more quickly than something that’s already stood the test of time”.
articles.author: Harry Roberts

articles.title: Considerations for Making a Tree View Component Accessible
articles.description: A look behind the scenes at GitHub’s attempts to make the tree view on GitHub repos be more accessible. It’s a surprisingly complex thing to get right.
articles.author: Eric Bailey (GitHub)

articles.title: So, You Want to Push a Web Platform Feature?
articles.description: If you’re curious about browser development Yoav shares some advice on why you may want to contribute, and how to go about doing so.
articles.author: Yoav Weiss

articles.title: 🎲 Some Things You Might Not Know About Custom Counter Styles
articles.description: Outlines how @counter-styles opens up new ways of working with lists and list markers.
articles.author: Geoff Graham

articles.title: The Speed Trifecta: 11ty, Brotli 11, and CSS Fingerprinting
articles.description: Matt explores a blended approach to optimizing CSS by combining Brotli compression and CSS fingerprinting, delivering the gains via a custom 11ty shortcode.
articles.author: Matt Hobbs

articles.title: 🤖 Running Inference in Web Extensions
articles.description: Firefox Nightly is shipping with an 'AI runtime' API you can use for offline machine learning tasks in Web extensions. It uses Transformers.js and is already used in Firefox 133 to provide alt text for images in PDFs.
articles.author: Tarek Ziadé (Mozilla)

articles.title: Positioning Text Around Elements with CSS Offset
articles.description: Explores how CSS offset can offer an easy option for adding pleasing text along borders, textual annotations, etc.
articles.author: Preethi Sam

articles.title: Squish: Batch Client-Side Image Compression Powered by Wasm
articles.description: Includes support for AVIF, JPEG, JPEGXL, PNG, and WebP. You can install it locally or try it in the browser here. Allows quality adjustment, batch processing, and real-time preview, among other features.
articles.author: Addy Osmani

articles.title: Unpic 1.0: A Toolkit for Displaying Images on the Web
articles.description: A family of components and libraries for working with images on the Web, whether it’s through components for many different frameworks or working with images hosted on many different providers and CDNs.
articles.author: Matt Kane

articles.title: Prompts: A Lightweight Async Alternative to alert(), prompt(), and confirm()
articles.description: Includes some basic styling for the prompts, which are like modals, and they’re designed to be keyboard-friendly and based on JS Promises.
articles.author: Simon Willison

articles.title: Blendy: Smoothly Transition One Element Into Another
articles.description: The demo is essentially an animated modal window but there could be other applications for this. It works with any framework and the code is simply a few lines defining the source and target elements.
articles.author: Taha Shashtari
